newsitem.title: USA: NY-NJ Port Authority might delay airport bond sale.
newsitem.headline: NY-NJ Port Authority might delay airport bond sale.

text.p: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey might delay the sale of $932 million of airport improvement bonds until next week, an official with lead underwriter Lehman Brothers said on Monday.
The Lehman official, who declined to be named, said the syndicate was checking with institutional buyers to see if they would like more time to review the sales documents.
The bonds will pay for a new international arrivals building at John F. Kennedy International Airport in the borough of Queens in New York city.
The sale, previously delayed from the first quarter because of the project's complexity, had been rescheduled for Wednesday.

Asked why it might be delayed again, the official replied: "Because we're trying to balance two things -- the need to finance the project as quickly as possible with the need to make sure that investors have enough time to review the credit."
Sales materials were not mailed until Friday.

The syndicate expects to decide on a new date by late Tuesday, after it has spoken with more big players. If the sale goes ahead this week, it would probably take place on Thursday or Friday, the Lehman official said.
No retail order period is planned, though the entire offering will be covered by bond insurance, which makes the deal much more attractive for individuals.
